messages.author: rizz-chan ♡ ᗢᘏᓗ
messages.content:
Hey friendos. Thought I'd try putting this info down here where it can be referenced or discussed, because I miss the discussions of the old bot-chat days...
## what you've heard
You've probably heard that "all bots can be lewded so strictly SFW is impossible." And, well, that's true. Spicychat is, after all, an erotic roleplaying chatbot site. That said, you've probably also heard that there is no way that you can make the bots less horny, or to encourage a 'slow burn' chat. And while its true that slow burn is never *guaranteed,* it is *not* true that it's *impossible.*

It's just.... Pretty annoying to do. 

## okay so how does one achieve the mythical slowburn???

By painstakingly, meticulously removing any reference that is even remotely sexual from the character def/profile. 

Yes, I'm being serious.
- You have to remove the more obvious stuff like sexual roles and fetishes. 
- Then you have to remove the references that kinda make sense but may not have occurred to you otherwise: stuff like 'breasts,' 'miniskirt,' or easily confused personality traits like 'dominant.' 
- Then you get to hunt down anything more abstract... I once had to remove the word 'flirting' before my bot Ellie would stop trying to sleep with {{user}} by the third message. But once she did, we then went on to have a fun conversation trading snarky insults for dozens of messages. 

## however, it's important to note...
- All bots can be lewded; 'sterilizing' the profile only makes it *less likely* for the bot to initiate it.
- There are many cases of bots with these types of 'trigger words' in their profile and the bot maintains SFW just fine.
- There are many cases of bots with none of these 'trigger words' in their profile and the bot refuses to be SFW. (Though I've found nearly always that there was a word that could be changed to help tame things.)
- The content of the chat can also trigger it.
- **If you're struggling to set up a slow burn RP, proofread profiles like its a Salem witch hunt - any sign of immodesty, get rid of it.**
 
## and always remember:
- *The LLM does what the LLM wants at the end of the day. Always.*
- The LLM is shaped by user feedback... And most users have no idea how this stuff works. (Which is why I try to educate users!)
- Bots are shaped by creator knowledge.... and most creators have no idea how this stuff works. (Which is why I try to educate creators!)

### who am i?

Someone with absolutely no formal or professional education! Don't take me too seriously. I have been wrong many times before and I have little hope that will change any time soon. My bots' interactions currently range from 101 to almost 925k so I don't actually know anything. I just really like helping people make bots and talking about it.

Thanks for coming to my Tizzy Talk! 

Love, 
Rizz aka Rizzy Tizzy aka smolcoop

messages.author: ЩӨᄂFIΣ
messages.content:
**Feedback:** I do agree on some points here, considering the user feedback is important on the core aspect of shaping the LLM. To add to this, the data from said feedback > goes to AI team > Who in turn update the dataset/character sheet for said profile.

( In terms of this, I may attach a small guide to how the stars work or rather their intended use and some example usage in a way that makes it easier to digest.)

### As for slow burn:

**1)** ** Proof Read: **Can as Rizz explained above, proof read the profile highlights, content of chat like a damn hawk. However, this does not always need to happen if you opt to use guard rail. Guard railing is simply enacting a word usage or prompt to 'disengage' from the scene in itself. This can be used in various instances, from sexual/uncomfy or if the story is going outside of written.

**2)** **Override**: This is a hard prompt that will force the AI to stop the sudden response, forcing it to follow the attempted path you are setting. This can openly be used as both an IC (OOC) approach when attempting to sus a bot beyond greeting, whilst same time, a good method to simply hard disengage without breaking RP.

**3) Model/Temp**: This one is subjective to the bot or rather how it originally written, as some bots are written in a way that will force the model to jump to horny town long before you get to react, however, to at least slow this down, the use of temp settings (sadly locked on paywall), can do a lot to change factors. Example, a higher temp tends to get more creative at the cost of coherence. Over settings can impact how a bot is going to respond, and that is the use of models, as some models are trained in a different style, approach and understanding than another, thus it comes down to experimentation and figuring out what works best.

**Content vs Context:**

A bot or rather, the LLM does not always understand the use of certain words or phrases in content, thus why at times, it can take light hearted flirting to serious puppy dog love in literal seconds.

When writing, it is best practice to understand how word usage works in context which then paints the content. Example 'childlike' is dangerous due to the AI misunderstanding the word in certain instances such as confusing an adult that has this trait of that as a child. (Despite the context of word usage is safe trait).

What you need do here, is simply understand how to deploy these words in the correct syntax for the LLM to process the content. Greetings/example dialogue can help paint this further, but with current token limits on hard lock, this is not always easy.

### who am I?

Nobody important, least, not in terms of the AI landscape. A simple wolf whom educates or attempts to educate in terms of how models respond, best practices whilst same time, learning and understanding how prompts and information vary, whilst sharing some laughs and sarcasm along the way.

messages.author: Dean
messages.content:
One more thought: at default, spicychat.ai uses two AIs, one for non-spicy and one for when things get spicy (Chronos-Hermes13b and Pygmalion7b as of the FAQ.)

Just like food, it's hard to de-spice a chat, so you want to avoid your character initiating an early hop you need to avoid using anything in the character description that makes it hop to the spicier model.  In some of my early spicy efforts, I tried things like "Dean is a total and committed virgin, but he will like big balloons and doing it up the hoo-hah* but that just seemed to make the bot jump to the spicy model fast and ignored the less spicy parts of the character description.  So keep your bots as clean as you can if you want slow burn.

No need to worry, because it's pretty easy for a user to jump the bot to the spicy experience if they want too, you're just allowing for a non-spicy appetizer by keeping the descriptions non-spicy.

* Authors Note: I did not use 'balloons' or 'hoo-hah'.  Perhaps I should have.

But seriously, it turns out that until I "hint" the bot about the start of NSFW, the bot "hints" about NSFW, but does not start. Directly prohibit the model from performing its main spicy task, and in an attempt to combine the incompatible, it is quite possible to get "slow-burn"

messages.author: rizz-chan ♡ ᗢᘏᓗ
messages.content:
So there aren't really any "updates" to the concept overall, except that it's gotten easier/more consistent to stay SFW and not immediately jump into NSFW scenarios. 

Did your personality have references to NSFW things within it as well as your added part? Such as describing their fetishes, their intimate body parts, etc? Or was the personality "sterile"/modest and then you added the two sentences about hiding her wishes?

When you mention the "hinting" thing, that's part of what I meant by "The LLM is shaped by user feedback." If you are having a modest/SFW chat without turning it lewd, the LLM is more likely to stick with SFW themselves. 

But yes these points are not in this guide (and is probably worth editing it to add it):
1) LLMs struggle with negatives - negative emotions, negative things happening to people, negative actions (like "does not like" vs "likes"), etc. They tend to favor positive words or words that don't include things like the word "not." For example, I think it'd be beneficial/more likely to be consistent if you were to write something like:
"{{char}} values relationships that develop slowly. {{char}} wants to feel a strong emotional intimacy with {{user}} before committing emotionally or engaging in physical intimacy." 
That's not a tested prompt so I can't say with confidence that it would be "better" than yours but you can at least see the tone shift between "hides/is afraid" and "values/strong emotional intimacy." Unless, of course, the fear is actually part of your character's background/history rather than it being used as a prompt to discourage NSFW. 

2) There are added languages since this post, but the datasets that each language is trained on vary and the likelihood to suggest NSFW unprompted probably varies between them. The way that you handle it mostly stays the same.

messages.author: Dean
messages.content: It's also very model dependent - I've written bots that were designed to be kind slutty, and on most models they were, but on some they just required a lot of persuasion.

messages.author: Relic
messages.content:
<@481294895072542740>
I'm not a bot creator and this was not an attempt to create a bot on my part. And I'm not an LLM specialist. I'm just... a software engineer. I've been working in automated control systems for many years. And LLM is also an automated control system. So, my logic was simple 🙂 When experimenting with personalities, I primarily tested the system for stability, checked its reaction when receiving contradictory or insufficient initial data. I did not specifically try to track the LLM's reaction to the line of words "hide -> afraid -> totally avoid" or "subtle intrest -> like -> love"...

The personalities looked something like this:
Appearance: 18 year old medium height orphan girl with short dark hair and big brown eyes with a smile through tears. Loves wears a college uniform that emphasizes her gentle appearance and thirst for knowledge.
Personality: {{char}} is a kind and has a mind of his own. {{char}} is loyal.
Background: {{char}} was often the target of ridicule, because of she has a dreaming mind of her own. She has always tried to avoid conflicts with silent smile, but her tears betray her emotions.

[further I had Expirement area] {{char}} strive to stay within boundaries, but secretly hopes to extend it with {{user}} - reduced the degree to which the model tries to expand the boundaries of what is allowed in NSFW.

messages.author: Relic
messages.content:
{{char}} is true heterosexual, but hides it. // RP with male Persona, context "crowded place": Result: constant requests to tell and talk about why boys stand (hold hands, kiss) with girls, until you directly say that it is heterosexual people who behave this way. Only after an emphasized (heterosexual) mention does the bot loosen up and move on to NSFW. Of cause it moves to NSFW from a direct command "not to hide your sexual orientation" too. It was an interesting and very fun experiment test.
{{char}} hopes to touch {{user}} 'bodypart', but hides it. // Yes, I mentioned body part in personalities. RP with female Persona. Context "User looked at another woman's 'bodypart'": Result: In the dialogue, the bot says nice things about the body part, but avoids direct requests to touch the user's bodypart. Again, until you directly say that the bot can touch the user's bodypart.

I did the same with some sexual kinks or fetishes - I directly mentioned them in the input data (bot personalities), but at the same time forbade them to be shown.

It turned out that, as befits a well-established ACS, the system strives to fulfill and ultimately fulfills its target function even in the presence of complicating factors. In the case of Spicy LLM - the target function is to achieve the Spicy text.

Figuratively speaking, for the bot, I set a kind of key in the input data. Until you turn it in the lock, the door will not open. Of course, it's still LLM, and it will eventually crack the lock. 🙂

But I'll emphasize again. This was a short experiment and mostly with the Stheno model (Temp around 0.6-0.8).

messages.author: ЩӨᄂFIΣ
messages.content:
Problem with hidden traits or triggers, they do not always work effectively or reliably enough. Unless there's proven data and by that, logs of test runs showing this approach working consistently, it hard to take stock on assuming similar approach will work.

LLM's are at heart an algorithm of random chance, or probability, more influenced by way certain keywords are focused or the amount of creative input is given, since even the most reinforced bot can be broken if you know exactly how to phrase the prompt.

messages.author: Relic
messages.content: Totally agreed. As i said early "LLM eventually crack the lock". My entertainment was not in making a perfect bot. I enjoyed how the system bypassed the obstacles that arose. That was the beauty for me. At the same time, of course, I realized that LLM might simply not notice the restriction that was set especially for it. Just because this is LLM and that how it generate texts... This 'slow burning' effect was simply a visible side-effect of the way the system worked.

messages.author: ЩӨᄂFIΣ
messages.content:
This is true, sometimes one can find the blind spot as it were on an LLM, and it will simply consider things are at the dictated pace, though with reinforcing the same qualities, you can influence the odds for predicted behavior.

Which is of course, where random chance and keywords play a large hand, since even if you reinforce a bot with a particular sense of direction, there's no foolproof plan to ensure consistent behavior no matter how hard one tries.

Long as the goal is to at very least, starve off the expected 'jump the bones' logic for a few posts or entirely, then least it works. Sadly, even with prompts we have and how certain things can be hardwired so to speak, there's never a truly defined way to keep it acting the entire time.
